summary: Build passes (0 errors, 0 warnings). All 159 tests pass (2 skipped: live-download guard + tar.xz fixture). All 5 ACs are explicitly met. However, two defects are found that require a bounce: (1) the new FfprobeArchive code path (Step 8b) has zero unit test coverage in FfmpegProvisionerTests.cs — the developer's handoff notes explicitly requested QA exercise this path, but it is unexercisable on a Windows x64 host without unit tests; (2) on FfprobeArchive SHA-256 verification failure, targetDir is left in a partially-extracted state (main archive present, no ffprobe binary) while partialDir is deleted — inconsistent cleanup contract vs Step 7 where targetDir never exists on failure. Two lower-priority issues are also flagged (stale DownloadVersion in LiveSettingsService, missing FfprobeArchive.Sha256 assertion in manifest tests)."

comments.note: FfprobeArchive code path (Step 8b) has zero unit test coverage. FfmpegProvisionerTests.cs has 6 test cases but none set FfprobeArchive on the ToolManifestEntry. Developer handoff notes explicitly asked QA to 'exercise the FfprobeArchive code path (macOS-style two-archive download)' — this path is entirely unexercisable on a Windows x64 host without unit tests. Required: add at minimum (a) a success-path test asserting FakeToolDownloader is called twice, extractor called twice, and FfprobePath equals Path.Combine(targetDir, FfprobeArchive.RelativePath); and (b) a checksum-mismatch test for the secondary archive. The existing fake/stub infrastructure in FfmpegProvisionerTests.cs supports this without new fixtures.

FfprobeArchive SHA-256 failure leaves targetDir in a partially-extracted state. In FfmpegProvisioner.cs Step 8b (around line 225), when ffprobeChecksumOk is false, only DeleteDirectoryIfExists(partialDir) is called — targetDir (which already contains the main archive extraction) is left on disk with only ffmpeg present but no ffprobe. This is inconsistent with Step 7's contract: when the MAIN archive checksum fails, targetDir never exists (it is created in Step 8 after Step 7 passes). Fix: also call DeleteDirectoryIfExists(targetDir) in the FfprobeArchive checksum failure branch to maintain a clean-failure invariant.

LiveSettingsService.DownloadVersion in FfmpegProvisionerLiveTests.cs (line 170) is 'n7.1' — stale since DownloadVersion was updated to 'n7.1.4' in appsettings.json. This means the live test caches binaries under tools/ffmpeg/n7.1/win-x64/ instead of tools/ffmpeg/n7.1.4/win-x64/, which is inconsistent with what the production application would create. Functionally harmless because a temp directory is used, but it reduces test fidelity. Fix: change DownloadVersion to 'n7.1.4'.

AppsettingsJson_Manifest_Sha256ValuesAreHexStrings in FfmpegManifestOptionsTests.cs only validates entry.Sha256 (the main archive hash). It does not validate entry.FfprobeArchive?.Sha256 for osx-x64 and osx-arm64. Two additional SHA-256 values exist in the manifest that carry the same format requirement but are not asserted. Fix: add a separate assertion that when entry.FfprobeArchive is non-null, its Sha256 also matches ^[0-9a-f]{64}$.

comments.note: A06 — Vulnerable & Outdated Components (Low). BtbN archive URLs are pinned to autobuild-2026-05-06-13-32. Already documented by Developer as debt. A periodic manifest refresh procedure is needed to pick up security patches in future FFmpeg 7.1.x point releases. No CVEs identified against the currently pinned build at time of review.

A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring Failures (Low). TarXzArchiveExtractor performs no audit logging for extraction start, Tar-Slip guard triggers, or extraction completion. This is a pre-existing gap already documented in the source file (TODO comment) as a prior Security Auditor finding. Not introduced by this WP. Recommend adding ILogger<TarXzArchiveExtractor> injection with LogDebug/LogWarning/LogInformation events as described in the class-level TODO.

A08 — Software & Data Integrity: Zip-Slip and Tar-Slip guards are present and correct in both ZipArchiveExtractor and TarXzArchiveExtractor. ZipArchiveExtractor uses Path.GetFullPath + StartsWith(OrdinalIgnoreCase) guard. TarXzArchiveExtractor additionally rejects symbolic links and hard links unconditionally. Both guards reviewed and confirmed effective. No finding — recorded as positive assurance.

A03 — Injection: Archive filename extraction in FfmpegProvisioner uses Path.GetFileName(new Uri(url).LocalPath). Uri.LocalPath normalises the URL path, and Path.GetFileName strips all directory separators, preventing path traversal in the staged archive filename. Confirmed safe for all five manifest URL patterns.

Info — A09: HttpToolDownloader logs full download URLs at LogInformation level (FfmpegProvisioner lines ~130 and ~210). Current manifest URLs contain no authentication tokens or credentials. If future provisioning sources required authenticated URLs (e.g., bearer tokens embedded in query strings), logging must be updated to redact them. Not an active risk; recorded as a forward-looking note.

comments.note: ComputeHex in FfmpegProvisionerTests.cs uses Convert.ToHexString() which returns uppercase hex, while the production convention (and the appsettings.json format) is lowercase. Works correctly because Sha256ChecksumVerifier performs case-insensitive comparison (documented on the Sha256 property), but creates a subtle inconsistency in test fixtures vs. production manifest values. Consider using BitConverter.ToString(SHA256.HashData(data)).Replace("-","").ToLowerInvariant() or Convert.ToHexString().ToLowerInvariant() to align conventions.

The property-level XML doc explains this, but the class-level doc should be updated to note this design trade-off and why FfprobeRelativePath remains required (backward compatibility, avoids nullable cascade to all existing manifest entries).
